title: Composition Pasting Coherence
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring and use the derived constant-$B$ strict-tower operations and normalized proper/open comparisons $\gamma$, open comparisons $\beta$, and proper-square mates $E$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension, lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of schemes with a supplied compatible tower [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]
$$X\xrightarrow a\overline X\xrightarrow p\overline Y\xrightarrow qZ,\qquad Y\xrightarrow i\overline Y.$$
Here $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ has projections $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p_Y:U\to Y$, and $c:X\hookrightarrow U$, with $bc=a$, $p_Yc=f$, and cartesian square $Q=(b,i,p_Y,p)$. The displayed open maps are quasi-compact and $p,q,p_Y$ proper. Put $F_f=R_{p_Y}^{\mathcal T}J_c$, $F_h=R_q^{\mathcal T}J_i$, $F_{hf}=R_{qp}^{\mathcal T}J_a$. On towers whose $n$-th evaluations are restrictions of finite-coefficient bounded-below etale-origin complexes [def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport],
$$D=R_q^{\mathcal T}\gamma_QJ_c:F_hF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{hf}$$
is a natural isomorphism, using the canonical proper-direct-image and open-extension compositors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].
For two such towers indexed by $1,2$, let a refinement from $1$ to $2$ consist of proper maps $u:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $w:U_1\to U_2$, satisfying $ui_1=i_2$, $va_1=a_2$, $wc_1=c_2$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $p_2v=up_1$, $p_{Y,2}w=p_{Y,1}$, $q_2u=q_1$. Define the three refinement maps $C_f,C_h,C_{hf}$ by $\gamma$ for the squares $(c_1,c_2,1_X,w)$, $(i_1,i_2,1_Y,u)$, $(a_1,a_2,1_X,v)$, followed by the corresponding proper direct images. Then the actual strict-tower transformations satisfy
$$C_{hf}D_2=D_1(C_hF_{f,1})(F_{h,2}C_f).$$
For a base change $g:Z'\to Z$ and its pullbacks $g_Y,g_X$, let $e_f:G_{g_Y}F_f\to F_f'G_{g_X}$, $e_h:G_gF_h\to F_h'G_{g_Y}$, and $e_{hf}:G_gF_{hf}\to F_{hf}'G_{g_X}$ each be the proper mate followed by the open comparison. The vertical interchange identity is
$$e_{hf}(G_gD)=(D'G_{g_X})(F_h'e_f)(e_hF_f).$$
Consequently $D$ and this identity transport unchanged through the above refinement maps and through any common refining compatible tower. These equalities hold before evaluation, with canonical composition identifications inserted.

proof.text:
Write $R_t=R_t^{\mathcal T}$ and suppress only the canonical compositors of the two operation definitions. Evaluation commutes with $J_c$. If $\operatorname{ev}_nM\cong C_X\nu_X^*L_n$, the normalized finite scalar/open transport and the etale/pro-etale open comparison give
$$\operatorname{ev}_nJ_cM\cong C_U\nu_U^*(c^{\mathrm{et}}_!L_n).$$
Here scalar restriction changes only the action on the extension presheaf, and the forward open comparison is the inverse open-adjunction comparison specified in the finite-transport definition. The comparison for sheaves extends degreewise to complexes, since the extensions and scalar transport are exact. Exactness of etale extension implies $H^t(c_!L_n)=c_!H^t(L_n)$, so the witness is bounded below with the same bound as $L_n$. Thus $J_cM$ meets precisely the finite-origin hypothesis of the strict-tower calculus. No common bound or common finite coefficient ring over all levels is required.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), first paragraph; pro-etale finite-origin typing via the cited comparison nodes

proof.text:
Apply the invertibility assertion of the strict-tower calculus to $Q$, at $J_cM$ as typed in step 1. Its proper maps are $p_Y,p$ and its quasi-compact open maps are $b,i$, exactly as supplied. Whiskering its natural isomorphism by $R_q$ and using $J_bJ_c\cong J_a$ and $R_qR_p\cong R_{qp}$ gives
$$R_qJ_iR_{p_Y}J_c\xrightarrow{R_q\gamma_QJ_c}R_qR_pJ_bJ_c\cong R_{qp}J_a.$$
This is the stated $D$, natural in $M$. All identifications have the normalized adjunction compositors of the operations; their compatibility with the canonical direct-image compositor is part of the calculus statement.

For the refinement write $r_j=p_{Y,j}$. Denote by $A$ the square with top $c_1$, bottom $c_2$, left $1_X$, right $w$; by $H$ the square with top $i_1$, bottom $i_2$, left $1_Y$, right $u$; and by $T$ the square with top $b_1$, bottom $b_2$, left $w$, right $v$. Write their comparisons as $\gamma_A,\gamma_H,\gamma_T$. These are permitted proper/open squares: the four refinement equations give commutativity and the stated properness and quasi-compact openness supply every hypothesis. In particular $T$ need not be cartesian. The horizontal pasting of $A$ and $T$ is the square with top $a_1$, bottom $a_2$, left $1_X$, right $v$. The horizontal law therefore gives
$$\gamma_a=(\gamma_TJ_{c_1})(J_{b_2}\gamma_A). \tag{1}$$
The refinement maps are, with these same compositors,
$$C_f=R_{r_2}\gamma_A,\quad C_h=R_{q_2}\gamma_H,\quad C_{hf}=R_{q_2}R_{p_2}\gamma_a.$$
The last targets are identified using $r_2w=r_1$, $q_2u=q_1$ and $p_2v=up_1$.

proof.text:
The vertical pasting of $T$ above $Q_2$ and the vertical pasting of $Q_1$ above $H$ have the same outer square: top $b_1$, bottom $i_2$, left $r_1=r_2w$, right $p_2v=up_1$. Apply the vertical law to both. It yields the equality with source $J_{i_2}R_{r_1}$ and target $R_{p_2}R_vJ_{b_1}\cong R_uR_{p_1}J_{b_1}$,
$$(R_{p_2}\gamma_T)(\gamma_{Q_2}R_w)=(R_u\gamma_{Q_1})(\gamma_HR_{r_1}). \tag{2}$$
Every vertical is proper ($w,v,r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2,u,1_Y$); every horizontal here is one of the given quasi-compact opens. This invokes the calculus for general commutative squares, including $T$, rather than its cartesian special case.

proof.text:
Naturality of $\gamma_{Q_2}:J_{i_2}R_{r_2}\to R_{p_2}J_{b_2}$ at the morphism $\gamma_A:J_{c_2}\to R_wJ_{c_1}$ gives
$$(R_{p_2}J_{b_2}\gamma_A)(\gamma_{Q_2}J_{c_2})=(\gamma_{Q_2}R_wJ_{c_1})(J_{i_2}R_{r_2}\gamma_A). \tag{3}$$
Indeed at each $M$ this is exactly the naturality square for $\gamma_{Q_2}$ with the two objects $J_{c_2}M$ and $R_wJ_{c_1}M$ of $D(\mathcal T_{U_2})$. Thus it is an equality of strict-tower derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, proof, interchange of squares A and B; Tag 0F7F discussion of natural transformations

proof.text:
Expand $C_{hf}D_2$ using (1), then (3), then (2). With composition read right to left this is
$$\begin{aligned}
C_{hf}D_2
&=R_{q_2}\big[(R_{p_2}\gamma_TJ_{c_1})(R_{p_2}J_{b_2}\gamma_A)(\gamma_{Q_2}J_{c_2})\big]\\
&=R_{q_2}\big[(R_{p_2}\gamma_TJ_{c_1})(\gamma_{Q_2}R_wJ_{c_1})(J_{i_2}R_{r_2}\gamma_A)\big]\\
&=R_{q_2}\big[(R_u\gamma_{Q_1}J_{c_1})(\gamma_HR_{r_1}J_{c_1})(J_{i_2}R_{r_2}\gamma_A)\big]\\
&=D_1(C_hF_{f,1})(F_{h,2}C_f).
\end{aligned}$$
The last line uses $R_{q_2}R_u=R_{q_1}$ and the definitions in step 3. Functoriality and associativity justify expanding and regrouping. Parenthesization independence in the calculus ensures that the same canonical identifications are used at each line. The named direct-image compositors are those of lem-cbc-strict-tower-direct-image-coherence. Its associativity identifies the two outer proper composites; the right identity law is obtained by conjugating the existing inverse-image right-unit law.

proof.text:
For base change write $t:\overline Y'\to\overline Y$, $s:\overline X'\to\overline X$, $d:U'\to U$, $y=g_Y$, and $x=g_X$. The compatible-tower statement supplies the pulled-back tower and the corresponding cartesian faces. Put $r=p_Y$. In these notations let
$$E_q:G_gR_q\to R_{q'}G_t,\quad E_p:G_tR_p\to R_{p'}G_s,\quad E_r:G_yR_r\to R_{r'}G_d.$$
The proper mate for $qp$ is $(R_{q'}E_p)(E_qR_p)$: this is pasting along the proper adjunctions, clause 2 of mate-pasting, applied to the two pullback squares and the normalized inverse-image compositors. Likewise the open comparison for $a=bc$ is $(J_{b'}\beta_c)(\beta_bJ_c)$ by the open-composition law of the calculus. Consequently
$$e_{hf}=(R_{q'}R_{p'}J_{b'}\beta_c)(R_{q'}R_{p'}\beta_bJ_c)(R_{q'}E_pJ_bJ_c)(E_qR_pJ_bJ_c). \tag{4}$$
This identifies the specified proper-then-open map, with no appeal to its evaluations. The canonical proper-mate pasting used here is strictTowerMatePasting of lem-cbc-strict-tower-direct-image-coherence, with the equality rCompEq_eq identifying its named compositor with the displayed rComp followed by equality transport.

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0E46/0E47, pasting as the cited mate theorem

proof.text:
Apply the base-change equation in the strict-tower calculus to $Q=(b,i,r,p)$ and the base change $t$. Its other projections are exactly $s,y,d$. It gives
$$(R_{p'}\beta_b)(E_pJ_b)(G_t\gamma_Q)=(\gamma_{Q'}G_d)(J_{i'}E_r)(\beta_iR_r). \tag{5}$$
Both sides start at $G_tJ_iR_r$ and end at $R_{p'}J_{b'}G_d$. The base-change map $t$ is arbitrary; no properness or smoothness of $g$ is required. The properness and quasi-compact openness hypotheses are those of $Q$ and its supplied pulled-back tower.

In $e_{hf}(G_gD)$, first use naturality of $E_q$ at $\gamma_QJ_c$ to move that factor inside $R_{q'}$. Formula (4) makes the result
$$R_{q'}\big[(R_{p'}J_{b'}\beta_c)(R_{p'}\beta_bJ_c)(E_pJ_bJ_c)(G_t\gamma_QJ_c)\big](E_qJ_iR_rJ_c).$$
Substitute (5), whiskered by $J_c$. Naturality of $\gamma_{Q'}$ at $\beta_c:G_dJ_c\to J_{c'}G_x$ says
$$(R_{p'}J_{b'}\beta_c)(\gamma_{Q'}G_dJ_c)=(\gamma_{Q'}J_{c'}G_x)(J_{i'}R_{r'}\beta_c).$$
The previous expression is therefore
$$R_{q'}\big[(\gamma_{Q'}J_{c'}G_x)(J_{i'}R_{r'}\beta_c)(J_{i'}E_rJ_c)(\beta_iR_rJ_c)\big](E_qJ_iR_rJ_c).$$
Its first factor is $D'G_x$, its next two factors are $F_h'e_f$, and its remaining factors are $e_hF_f$. This is exactly the asserted vertical interchange identity. The calculation only uses naturality and the cited strict-tower identity (5).

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change), applied inside the composition construction of Tag 0F7J

proof.text:
For the refinement square with top $a_1$, bottom $a_2$, left $1_X$, right $v$, the finite-origin clause of the calculus applied to $M$ makes $C_{hf}$ invertible. Step 2 makes both $D_j$ invertible. Hence step 6 makes $H=(C_hF_{f,1})(F_{h,2}C_f)=D_1^{-1}C_{hf}D_2$ invertible, without a separate finite-origin assumption on $F_fM$.
The calculus cube applied to the three refinement squares gives $C'_\bullet e_{\bullet,2}=e_{\bullet,1}(G C_\bullet)$ for $f,h,hf$: the cube equation is on all inputs, even when the isomorphism assertion is restricted. Naturality of $e_h$ with $C_f$ then gives
$$H'G_x\,(F_{h,2}'e_{f,2})(e_{h,2}F_{f,2})=(F_{h,1}'e_{f,1})(e_{h,1}F_{f,1})(G_gH).$$
Substitute this equality and $C'_{hf}e_{hf,2}=e_{hf,1}G_gC_{hf}$ into step 9, together with $C_{hf}D_2=D_1H$ and its primed version; the identity is thereby identified under refinement. The compatible-tower theorem supplies a common refining tower for any two choices. For its two maps the preceding equations identify both $D$ and step 9. The refinement/exchange theorem, applied only to the compactifications of $hf$ at $M$, gives independence and the cocycle of the $C_{hf}$ comparisons. Since $H=D_1^{-1}C_{hf}D_2$, these properties also hold for the corresponding horizontal comparisons. Thus the transport is independent of the common refinement. Every equality used is before evaluation. Lean implementation note (D2): compositionRefinement_isIso factors the hf comparison through the identity-left gamma and canonical isomorphisms, then cancels D_1 using the refinement clause of compositionPastingCoherence. compositionRefinementExchange applies the declared refinement/exchange theorem to f, h and hf, and uses naturality to combine the first two squares. Its transformation equalities do not depend on the finite-origin input demanded by other conjuncts of that theorem: a genuine zero finite-origin object, constructed with the finite zero coefficient ring, supplies that input. For common-refinement independence, apply refinementExchangeCoherence to hf to identify the second comparison. The refinement square already proved identifies the first comparison uniquely after cancellation of the invertible D. Thus equality of the pair does not require an additional common-refinement existence construction.
